_what_this_is: AutoSync's own survivor list for tools/proving.py (the ERP's prover pointed at this repository, AP11).
A survivor is a deliberate change no check noticed. Each one here has the reason no check can ever notice it;
a survivor not listed here is a failure, and an entry that no longer survives is a failure too (the prover says STALE).
The question every reason answers: is there any state a check could reach in which what is written, what is
stored, or what the seller is told comes out different? `cannot_load` names, per file, the changes that stop the
checks file loading at all -- noticed, but by the file failing to load rather than by a check going red.

accepted.why: The return after carryOnWaiting in the ask-again alarm branch. Without it the code falls to the next line, which returns for every alarm that is not the daily one, and the ask-again alarm is not the daily one. The same nothing is started, stored or shown either way (AJ8).

The only caller uses the page size as `size && notTheLast()`, and notTheLast needs pagesNamed() above 0. pagesNamed returns 0 for every way with no pageLabel, so for such a way the size is never acted on whether it is 0 or the printed number. For a way with a pageLabel the line does not return. No wait, no failure, no row read or put away comes out different.

accepted.line: if column == "settlement" and str(was) != "" and not added:
accepted.why: Deleting this line puts the line under it (figure_replaced = True) inside the block above, whose condition is this one with `reading.only_existing` added. Only a payments reading carries a settlement, and every payments reading is only_existing, so for every reading this package makes the two conditions are the same and nothing written, stored or said changes. Checked by payments_checks 'A SKU LINE THAT LEAVES THE FIGURE AS IT IS AND CHANGES A CHARGE CLEARS NO FEE KEY' (AP11), which passes either way for that reason.

This is inside `if figure_replaced and ...`, and figure_replaced is only ever set on a line right after `changed[name] = True` has already run for the same row in the same pass. Deleting this one leaves changed[name] True all the same, so the row is written exactly as before; there is no state in which it differs.

The `continue` after an unreadable Amazon settlement amount only saves work: without it the line falls through with no amount, its charge is not computed (it needs an amount), it is not counted as a no-order line (that needs an amount too), and _Lines.put returns at once for a line with no settlement and no charge. The unreadable text is already set aside by name above. No sale, charge, key or aside comes out different.

`holds` returns false for a missing outer or inner node whether the guard says `||` or `&&`: with outer missing the climb from inner ends at the top without ever meeting it, and with inner missing the loop never starts, so both give false; no state differs.

The guard only ever sees a missing node if a caller passes one, and none can: every caller (driver.js whatMatches, innermostOf, the row climbs, the month-heading climb) passes a node taken from a list of real nodes or an `up` that its own loop condition has just required to be present. Returning true instead of false for a missing node is therefore never reached.

Without the guard line a missing outer node makes the climb from inner run to the top of the page and give false, and a missing inner node skips the loop and gives false, which is exactly what the line returned; and no caller passes a missing node at all.

This is the last line of `holds` after the loop that returns true on a meeting; without it the function answers undefined instead of false, and every caller only asks whether the answer is truthy (inside `some` and `!`), so nothing written, stored or said changes.

accepted.line: if (made.getUTCFullYear() !== y || made.getUTCMonth() !== m - 1 || made.getUTCDate() !== d) return null;
accepted.why: `new Date(Date.UTC(y, m - 1, d))` that does not give the same day back always moves the year (a year below 100, or a month past twelve or below one) or moves the month and the day together (a day past the month's end or below one); a change of the month alone or of the day alone cannot happen. So `month !== m - 1 && day !== d` is true whenever `month !== m - 1 || day !== d` is, and the year test in front of it answers first for the rest.

When the Quality Recommendations heading is missing (`to < 0`) and the feedback heading is there, `to < from` is true as well, and when the feedback heading is later than the recommendations the section sliced between them is empty whether or not this guard returns first; so `from < 0 || (to < 0 && to < from)` and the original give an empty list for every page.

This is the `return false;` that ends the catch of closeWhatIsInTheWay. Deleting it makes the function return undefined instead of false. Every caller uses the result only as a truth value (`many === 0 && await ...`, `if (!(await ...)) throw blocked`), and undefined and false are both falsy, so no write, store or word to the seller differs.

The starting value is never read: walkThisPage is called only from walkAndReloadOnce, which sets somethingWasPressed = false on its first line of every turn before any step runs, and the only read is after that call. Starting at true instead of false leaves no state in which a result differs.

This only saves work: with no cell or one cell, the lines below either find no run to keep and answer the cells as they came, or keep the one cell (it is the only candidate), or keep nothing and fall back to the cells as they came (`kept.length > 0 ? kept : cells`). In every case the answer is those same cells, so nothing pressed, written or said comes out different.

accepted.line: try { if (chrome.permissions && chrome.permissions.remove) await chrome.permissions.remove({ permissions: ['nativeMessaging'] }); } catch (ignored) { /* already gone */ }
accepted.why: `chrome.permissions && chrome.permissions.remove` and `chrome.permissions || chrome.permissions.remove` take the same road in every state: with no permissions object both skip the call (undefined is falsy), with one that has a remove both make it, and with one that has no remove the changed test is true and calls undefined, which throws inside the try that swallows it. Nothing is written, stored or said differently (BR1).

Removing `frozen=True` from KeptFigure only allows assigning to its fields afterwards. Nothing assigns to a KeptFigure: plan() builds it once and hands it on, and the sibling classes in this file carry the same line. No state exists in which what is written, stored or said differs.

accepted.line: if column == "settlement" and name in only_a_fee:
accepted.why: The test only decides whether `fee_base_was` is set. `fee_base_was` is read only inside `if fee_keys and not fee_seen`, and `fee_keys` is empty for any row that is not in `only_a_fee`. Changing the test therefore changes a value that is never read in the rows it newly applies to (PR1c).

accepted.line: def _a_note_in_the_logs_folder(transport, inside: str) -> Callable[[str, str], None]:
accepted.why: No check reaches nightly's wiring of the before-history note onto the real Drive transport: it is one call to the already proven `_put_in_place` into the Logs folder. The callback the ledger calls is checked with a stand-in in ledger_sheet_checks (name, text, one note per file). First live night shows it. Weaker than the other reasons (PR1c).

Same function as the entry above: returning the note-keeping callback. Without it nightly would pass no callback and the before-history lines would be said in the log but no note file kept. No check reaches nightly's real Drive wiring; the callback itself is checked in ledger_sheet_checks. Weaker than the other reasons (PR1c).

accepted.line: if unwrapped is not body and landing.what_it_really_is(unwrapped) != landing.ZIP:
accepted.why: The second half of a defensive condition: the landing's unwrapper returns a spreadsheet, and an inner plain zip is refused by the reader's next step in words anyway. Not shown unreachable by a check; the first half is killed by the zip-with-one-spreadsheet checks (PR1 A4).

The return after 'Nothing has run yet.' in showTheEvents. Without it the code goes on to the loop over the events, and that list is empty (it is the only way into that branch), so the loop draws nothing. The panel shows the one 'Nothing has run yet.' line either way; nothing written, stored or said differs (AJ9).

It only makes `import move_group` find tools/. Run as a script (the workflow runs `python tools/move_group_on_release.py`), Python already puts the script's own folder first on the path, and the checks put tools/ there themselves. So the same move_group is found in every state and nothing moved, refused or said differs (AJ9).
